abstentions: I abstain from stating whether Pension Credit stops for a self-funding permanent care-home resident, because the package does not establish it.
I abstain from any individual entitlement decision or award calculation.
I abstain from assuming the claimant has no partner, or that partner status persists after admission.
I do not rely on historical amendment pages or the unrelated ADM/UC lexical matches as current rules.

evidence.quote:
Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)
78088 An additional amount for the severely disabled is applicable to a person who is permanently in a

care home if all the conditions are satisfied1.


Note: This will normally be self funding claimants, but DMs should be aware that it will also include
residents where the payment of “AA” or DLA/PiP continues for the first four weeks after admission.

claims.scope_or_qualification: This concerns only the severe-disability additional amount in the no-partner branch, not the whole Pension Credit award. All qualifying conditions must remain satisfied, including actual receipt of a qualifying benefit, no non-ignored co-resident adults, and no carer receiving CA or UC carer element. Self-funding status alone does not settle entitlement. The note refers to benefit payment continuing for four weeks after admission; it is not a four-week rule for the whole credit. Dated changes in memos 02/25, 06/25 and 01/26 add qualifying benefits and are not consolidated here.
claims.statement: Under the heading 'Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)', DMG 78088 states that the severe-disability additional amount is applicable to a person permanently in a care home if all the conditions are satisfied. The accompanying note says this will normally be self-funding claimants, and will also include residents whose AA or DLA/PiP payment continues for the first four weeks after admission.

evidence.quote:
Claimants who have a partner
78089 A member of a couple who is permanently in a care home is no longer a member of the same
household as their partner. In such a case each person may claim SPC as a claimant who has no partner.

77128 Where one of a couple is permanently in a care home or independent hospital (see DMG 77005 et
seq), that person is treated as not being a member of the same household as their partner (see DMG
77117 2.). But both partners, or all members of a polygamous marriage, may be permanently in a care
home or independent hospital. In such a case the DM must decide whether the partners, or members of
the polygamous marriage, are nevertheless members of the same household.

claims.scope_or_qualification: 'May claim' does not mean an award automatically follows; the entitlement conditions in DMG 77031 still apply. Partner status after admission is not assumed. The both-partners branch is a question of fact under DMG 77129–77130. Temporary absence is a separate branch.
claims.statement: Under DMG 78089 and 77128, a member of a couple who is permanently in a care home is treated as not being a member of the same household as their partner, and each person may claim State Pension Credit as a claimant who has no partner. Where both partners are permanently in a care home, the decision maker must decide whether they are nevertheless members of the same household.

evidence.quote:
78270 An additional amount for housing costs should not be allowed for


1. HB expenditure1 or


2. claimants in a care home, unless their absence from the dwelling normally occupied as their home is

temporary2 (see DMG 78240 et seq)

claims.scope_or_qualification: This concerns only the housing-cost additional amount, not the whole award. The temporary-absence rules are separate: trial periods of up to 13 weeks under DMG 78240, and 52-week absences under DMG 78254–78257. This paragraph says nothing about funding of care-home fees.
claims.statement: DMG 78270 states that the housing-cost additional amount should not be allowed for claimants in a care home unless their absence from the dwelling normally occupied as their home is temporary.

gaps: No captured provision states whether the whole Pension Credit award (Guarantee Credit or Savings Credit) stops or continues on a permanent care-home move, either for self-funders or generally.

Omitted items include the temporary-care-home and mixed-age domain records, guarantee-credit term, DMG 78/0021–0023 and 78/0054, Schedule I/II/III and regulation 5 legal bodies, and Chapter 85/84 related pages.
Rules on continuation or cessation of qualifying disability benefits (AA/DLA/PIP/ADP) after care-home admission, and their timing, are not supplied beyond the four-week note.

Legal version, commencement and territory are not reconciled; the dated memo changes (21.10.24, 21.3.25, 15.03.26) are not consolidated.

Unknown household facts: partner status, whether both partners are in a home, qualifying-benefit receipt, carer receipt, whether the stay is truly permanent, the funding arrangement, and whether there is a former home or housing costs.

summary: The package is truncated: node, relationship, byte and retrieval-candidate budgets omitted items. Its evidence status is insufficient. It does not contain a rule saying the whole Pension Credit award stops when a self-funding person moves permanently into a care home. Nor does it establish that the award continues in every such case. The captured DMG text supports three narrower points. First, under DMG 78088, headed 'Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)', the severe-disability additional amount can apply to a person permanently in a care home if all its conditions are satisfied. Second, under DMG 78089 and 77128, a member of a couple who is permanently in a care home is treated as no longer in the same household as their partner. Each person may then claim as a claimant with no partner, but where both partners are in a home the decision maker must decide the household question on the facts. Third, under DMG 78270, the housing-cost additional amount is not allowed for claimants in a care home unless the absence from home is temporary. These points concern additional amounts and household status, not the whole award. Applicability, current law, dated changes and specialist review remain unresolved. No individual decision or calculation is given.
